decision_2_3_bundled_mcp_vs_nfr1_now.decision_now: OPTION (a) -- the plugin bundles ZERO MCP servers, with an explicit opt-in registration command
decision_2_3_bundled_mcp_vs_nfr1_now.evidence_base_record: plugin_schema_spike.md item 5 -- two full process spawns in a session whose prompt explicitly forbade tool use, both logging the isolated session cwd
decision_2_3_bundled_mcp_vs_nfr1_now.primary_reason_record: Option (b) would make NFR-1 unfalsifiable. NFR-1 has already taken one carve-out (the retained Stop hook, ADR-018 consequence 3). With ADR-010 forbidding hooks and a second carve-out removing MCP, nothing would remain that could make NFR-1 fail. A metric that cannot fail measures nothing -- the project's primary success metric would pass by construction while the user's machine ran more processes than before.
secondary_reasons_record: The 13 MCP servers already exist as user-scope registrations; bundling duplicates registrations rather than reducing processes, so the plugin gains no operational capability it does not already have.

ADR-010's test (can the user decline?) transfers, and an explicit opt-in command cures the exact defect ADR-010 identified -- unlike a bundled .mcp.json, an opt-in command can be declined by not running it and reversed by running its inverse.
decision_2_3_bundled_mcp_vs_nfr1_now.pm_sizing_treated_as_record: cost data, not recommendation. PM's 'only (b) preserves the MVP boundary without rework' is accepted as accurate schedule data and explicitly rejected as a reason to redefine the metric.

addendum_findings_now.finding_as_filed: FR-23's MUST-PRECEDE-FR-4 ordering constraint, protecting the version-push gate closed by commit 1bb4303, is not mechanically enforced.
addendum_findings_now.response_now: ACCEPTED -- ADR-017 covers the ordering constraint. But ADR-019 changed WHERE the guarantee lives, and that is disclosed rather than left implicit.
addendum_findings_now.covered_now: AS OF 2026-08-01 THE CI ASSERTION IS DESIGNED, NOT BUILT. ADR-017 specifies it -- fail the build if the PreToolUse registration is absent while no MCP-side version-push gate is reachable by name, asserting on the REPLACEMENT rather than on the old hook's survival (polarity gate-verified). That specification is complete and correct. No such CI check exists in the repository today.
addendum_findings_now.what_changed_now: ADR-019 made MCP registration opt-in, moving WHERE the local guarantee would live. But the earlier wording here -- 'the CI assertion is the ONLY mechanical protection remaining' -- implied that one exists. IT DOES NOT. Corrected at consensus iteration 2.
addendum_findings_now.character_change_now: PREVENTIVE -> DETECTIVE. The gate no longer blocks a non-compliant push at push time; it fails the build afterwards. Adequate for a shared repository (nothing non-compliant merges); NOT equivalent for a developer's local history. Calling the two the same would be the softening this HLD has refused elsewhere.
addendum_findings_now.remaining_open_now: Preventive local protection, if wanted. Named as ADV-012 (git pre-push hook -- not a Claude Code hook, so ADR-010 does not apply; spawns only on explicit git push, so NFR-1-compatible). NAMED, NOT ADOPTED -- new scope belonging to FR-23's owner.

true_state_now.today_before_FR4_now: PROTECTED. push_gate.py still runs via the live PreToolUse hook; FR-4 has not been executed. The bypass commit 1bb4303 closed is currently closed.
true_state_now.after_FR4_if_neither_built_now: UNPROTECTED, preventively AND detectively. register-mcp does not exist, so there is no local MCP-side gate. The ADR-017 CI assertion does not exist, so there is no repository- level catch. Both are proposals.
true_state_now.detective_mechanism_now: ADR-017 CI assertion -- DESIGNED, NOT BUILT
true_state_now.implication_now: FR-23's MUST-PRECEDE-FR-4 ordering is therefore not merely unenforced by CI -- it has no mechanical enforcement of any kind pending both builds. This does NOT weaken ADR-017's design; it means the design must actually land before FR-4 is actioned, which is exactly what the ordering constraint says and exactly what nothing currently enforces.

A_manual_settings_edit.reason_record: The plugin ships no hooks (ADR-010) and Claude Code does not notify plugins of settings.json edits. Prevention is genuinely impossible without reintroducing a hook.
A_manual_settings_edit.control_now: DETECTION at next invocation -- doctor command plus a per-command start-up check. NFR-1-safe because ADR-006 means the plugin runs only when invoked.
A_manual_settings_edit.honest_label_record: unenforceable at edit time, documented deliberately -- NOT 'we wrote a doc and moved on'. Layer 2 bounds the undetected window to a single plugin invocation.

B_unregister_mcp.reason_record: unregister-mcp is a plugin-owned command that IS DESIGNED TO read and write settings.json per ADR-019 (design, not existing behaviour -- the command does not exist yet).
B_unregister_mcp.control_now: PREVENTION -- refuse by default when PreToolUse is absent, name the consequence, offer two ways forward (restore PreToolUse, or re-run with an explicit acknowledgement flag). Same shape as ADR-007's dev-mode guardrails: possible, never accidental.
B_unregister_mcp.significance_record: THIS PATH REACHES THE UNSAFE STATE WITHOUT PASSING THROUGH THE RUNBOOK AT ALL. A user who migrated correctly and later unregisters lands in the step-5-without-step-2 configuration having never reopened SS 10. Runbook wording gives zero coverage. This alone settles the question.

C_plugin_uninstall.interception_now: NONE (uninstall is Claude Code's command, not the plugin's)
C_plugin_uninstall.control_now: INFERRED to need none -- NOT measured. Verification task attached.
C_plugin_uninstall.status_correction_record: This entry previously asserted that user-scope registrations 'SURVIVE plugin uninstall' and that Path C needs 'NONE NEEDED', stated as fact. Both gates independently reached the same objection and the HLD's ADR-020 was corrected at Phase 2.4; this finding record was not, and kept asserting the claim its own fix retracted. Corrected at Phase 2.5 with the same four-part structure the HLD carries.
measured_record: Across a full install -> uninstall -> prune cycle the parsed-JSON structural diff reports 'changed keys: (none)'; the 5 hook registrations and 25 pre-existing mcpServers entries are byte-for-byte identical to baseline. Uninstall added enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces and emptied them; it changed nothing else.
The spike plugin's own .mcp.json server was NOT merged into the top-level mcpServers key at all -- it stayed plugin-scoped, tracked in the plugin manifest and installed_plugins.json.
C_plugin_uninstall.inferred_now: Uninstall manages plugin-scoped registrations in a DIFFERENT STORE from top-level mcpServers, and demonstrably does not alter that key's contents for anyone. register-mcp writes to top-level mcpServers (user scope), so an entry it writes should survive its own plugin's uninstall.
C_plugin_uninstall.not_measured_record: No entry written by register-mcp existed during the measured uninstall, because register-mcp does not exist yet. The 25 surviving entries were pre-existing and unrelated to the plugin. The spike shows uninstall does not remove UNRELATED entries; it does not show uninstall would not remove entries ATTRIBUTABLE to the plugin being uninstalled. That would require provenance tracking on a key that the second measured finding makes architecturally unlikely -- but unlikely is not measured.
C_plugin_uninstall.why_the_label_matters_now: If the inference is wrong, Path C is the ONLY path with no available control. Prevention is impossible (uninstall is Claude Code's command) and detection is impossible too -- the plugin is gone, so no doctor command and no per-command check can run. Every other path degrades to a weaker control; Path C degrades to none. The unhedged claim was concealing the highest-consequence uncertainty in the ADR.
C_plugin_uninstall.verification_task_now: Owner: whoever implements register-mcp. ~10 minutes, at the only moment it can be performed. Install the plugin, run register-mcp, run /plugin uninstall, confirm the written mcpServers entry is still present in settings.json. If it survives, Path C is measured safe and ADR-020 needs only a status update. If it does not, Path C acquires a control at that point -- and because no plugin-side control is possible, that control must be external: promote ADV-012's git pre-push hook from proposed to required, as the only mechanism surviving the plugin's own removal.
C_plugin_uninstall.conditional_benefit_now: IF the inference holds, ADR-019 also removed a failure mode nobody identified: had the servers been bundled, uninstall would have taken the push gate with them. Genuine second-order win, contingent on the verification above, NOT claimed as established.

addendum_findings_now.decision_now: ADR-020 -- three layers matched to what each path permits: (1) PREVENT on Path B via unregister-mcp refusal-by-default; (2) DETECT on Path A via doctor + per-command check; (3) PREVENT THE HARM rather than the config state via ADV-012's git pre-push hook if adopted, with ADR-017's CI assertion as detective backstop.
rejected_now: Leave the runbook as the only control -- repeats the DOCUMENTED-ONLY defect, and Path B proves runbook wording cannot cover a transition that bypasses the runbook.
unregister-mcp warns but proceeds -- a command that warns then does the thing is exactly how the 7 dead Stop-hook references failed.
unregister-mcp refuses absolutely with no override -- paternalistic, and contradicts ADR-019's own principle that the user must be able to decline. Agency is the point; accidents are the target.

Block all plugin commands while the unsafe state persists -- over-reach; the plugin would refuse unrelated work over a configuration it does not own, which is the involuntary blocking ADR-006 removed.

enumeration_now.finding_as_filed: FR-18's AC unachievable as written; BA owns the rewrite; two resolution paths sized here (FR-18a plugin-shipped cleanup command, +2 points).
enumeration_now.response_now: ACCEPTED on the AC rewrite (BA FIND-04, actioned). NEWLY ANSWERED at Phase 2.4 -- the FR-18a sizing sub-point was not previously responded to. ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT ON FR-18a: a PLUGIN-SHIPPED cleanup command cannot execute after the plugin is uninstalled, which is precisely when the residue exists (empty-but-present settings.json keys, orphaned unpruned cache dir). This is structurally identical to ADR-020 Path C -- once the plugin is gone, no plugin-side code can run. FR-18a is therefore viable ONLY as a pre-uninstall preparation step, which is a different capability from cleaning post-uninstall residue, or as an EXTERNAL script. FR-24's user-run cleanup runbook is the shape that actually works post-uninstall. RECOMMEND: PM re-scope FR-18a explicitly as pre-uninstall prep, or fold it into FR-24. Sizing it as a cleanup command implies a capability the architecture cannot deliver.

(1) A stale denominator relayed by the coordinator: 8 BA findings, predating FIND-09 and FIND-10. stale_review_artifact_class_now.finding_as_filed: Every fix this project produced was applied to hld.md and to nothing else. The finding records that prompted those fixes kept asserting the claims the fixes retracted. Three instances found at Phase 2.5, all in this file: the 'omitted 4' count, 'already reads and writes', and Path C stated as measured.
stale_review_artifact_class_now.root_cause_record: A review artifact reads as a historical record, so nobody treats it as something that can go stale. But sa_defence.json is not a changelog -- it states CURRENT POSITIONS, and a current position that has been superseded is simply wrong. The distinction that matters: a changelog QUOTES an old value (correct, and must not be edited); a position record ASSERTS a value (must be updated). This file contains both, which is why the error was easy to miss.
stale_review_artifact_class_now.relationship_to_other_classes_record: This is the backward-propagation class one layer out. The four earlier instances were hld.md-internal (SS 3 diagram, SS 10 runbook, SS 4 heading basis, coverage accounting). These three are hld.md-external -- the artifact is a different file entirely, which is why an ADR Affects list scoped to HLD sections would not have caught any of them.

_field_semantics_contract.purpose: Make the record-vs-claim distinction STRUCTURAL rather than a rule someone remembers. Four recurrences of the stale-review-artifact class happened in this file, including one in the same pass that added a self-diagnostic naming the risk. Writing down a tendency did not prevent it. The field NAME must now answer 'is this a record or a claim?'

suffix_rules._as_filed / _record: FROZEN. A quotation of what was said, or of what was believed true, at the time of filing. NEVER edited. Cannot go stale, because it does not assert a present fact.
suffix_rules._now: LIVE. A current claim about the present state of the design or the codebase. MUST be re-verified on every pass and updated the moment it is superseded. If you cannot verify it this pass, say so IN the field rather than leaving it to age silently.
suffix_rules.metadata allowlist: Structural keys carrying no substantive claim (id, n, severity, phase, date...).

_field_semantics_contract.enforcement: validator_source below is the actual check, embedded so it is reproducible rather than described. Run it against this file before committing. It returns the list of fields in a claim-bearing container whose name does not classify itself; a non-empty list is a schema violation. A convention nobody can violate silently is the only kind that survives -- same reasoning as ADR-013's non-optional manifest argument and ADR-015's three-way union: the defect is made inexpressible rather than discouraged.
_field_semantics_contract.known_limitation: NONE REMAINING WITHIN THIS FILE. The convention now covers all 14 top-level sections, not the three finding arrays it originally covered. The residual limitation is one of kind rather than scope: the convention classifies FIELDS, so it guarantees that every claim declares whether it is frozen or live. It does NOT verify that a _now field's content is actually current -- only that its staleness is checkable rather than invisible. Keeping _now fields true is still work; the convention makes that work enumerable, which is what a manual sweep could never do.

validator_result_now.negative_test: REQUIRED, and run: an unclassified field was injected into the first container and the validator returned 1 violation(s), proving it is not a no-op. Adopted from the consensus gate's stress test, which went beyond what either party specified. A validator that always passes is indistinguishable from one that works; only trying to break it separates them. Any check FR-25 or FR-26 produces needs the same companion negative test, or it is a green light with no mechanism behind it.
validator_result_now.embedded_source_verified_now: The validator_source string above was exec'd and run against this document, not a local copy: 0 violation(s). Negative test injected an unclassified field into meta and the SAME embedded source returned 1 violation(s), so the embedded string is itself proven non-trivial. This closes the gap where an embedded validator could drift out of sync with the scope it claims to check -- which would have been this very defect class inside the field designed to prevent it.

_field_semantics_contract.proof_it_works_record: On its first run the validator FAILED with 5 violations -- all of them fields this same pass had just added (true_state_now's children: today_before_FR-4, after_FR-4_if_neither_is_built, preventive_mechanism, detective_mechanism, and a bare as_of). The convention caught its own author adding unclassified fields, in the same edit that introduced the convention. That is the difference between a rule remembered and a rule enforced, and it is the evidence that the previous four recurrences were not a discipline problem.
